title: The Marks Themselves
label: ch:signos
canDo: I can name eight Spanish punctuation marks, say what each one does to a sentence, and write a short note that uses six of them correctly.

payoff.summary: Write a short note that opens with a colon after the name, lists three things without a comma before the final y, carries an aside in parentheses and an address abbreviated with a slash.
payoff.note: Eight points close at once, all from the Puntuacion category, which the coverage test names as the corpus's emptiest column at 1/9. Every one of these marks has been PRINTED by the corpus for hundreds of chapters and never once named: the dialogue raya opens every printed exchange in the book, including the ones chapters 421-423 added, and the corpus had never told the reader what it was. That is what makes this a teaching gap rather than a vocabulary gap -- the reader has been decoding these marks by guess. The comma lesson is the one with an exam consequence a marker can see: Spanish writes NO comma before the final y of a list, and an English-trained hand puts one there.
